WINNER: interest_signature_hypball
FIRST LISTED: transition-radial-sector-vq
ARGUMENT: (1) behavior_evidence: B’s proposed user-conditioned predecessor-cohort profile has direct train-only support: positive pairs share a successor cohort at 0.9291 versus 0.8871 for negatives, and profile overlap beats all ten negatives for 0.5898 of pairs (E9); A’s successor-entropy evidence supports predictability variation but does not directly validate its KL-sector signal. (2) novelty: B tests cross-user interest roles, a distinct signal from the measured successor-geodesic and tangent-successor mechanisms (E6–E7), whereas A remains closer to the already measured successor-profile/geodesic family. (3) geometry_necessity: neither establishes a matched Euclidean control, but B’s explicit cohort-conditioned tangent shift and restricted Poincaré assignment give a clearer, testable curved-vs-Euclidean comparison point (E12–E14).
FAILURE RISK: B’s deterministic hash cohorts may be arbitrary or too noisy to encode genuine interest; if they do not improve first-token survival or downstream Recall@10 over a matched Euclidean assignment, its behavioral premise and hyperbolic choice are unsupported.
